gloss: to stir up; to touch off; to create (a stir)

definitions.gloss: to stir up; to touch off; to whip up
definitions.explanation: To set off a reaction that spreads through a crowd or a society — debate, criticism, a craze, a sensation. The subject is usually a person, a work, or an event.

examples.japanese: {話題|わだい}を{巻|ま}き{起|お}こす。
その{発言|はつげん}は{大|おお}きな{議論|ぎろん}を{巻|ま}き{起|お}こした。
examples.english: That remark touched off a major debate.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}{監督|かんとく}の{作品|さくひん}が{映画|えいが}{界|かい}にブームを{巻|ま}き{起|お}こしている。
examples.english: A new director's film is setting off a boom in the movie world.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive. The reaction takes を; the person or thing that provokes it is the subject.
- The intransitive partner {巻|ま}き{起|お}こる means that the reaction arises by itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {議論|ぎろん}を{巻|ま}き{起|お}こす: to touch off a debate
- {物議|ぶつぎ}を{巻|ま}き{起|お}こす: to cause controversy
- ブームを{巻|ま}き{起|お}こす: to set off a craze
- {旋風|せんぷう}を{巻|ま}き{起|お}こす: to create a whirlwind, to take the field by storm

What gets stirred up is nearly always a collective reaction, so a single small incident is {起|お}こす, not {巻|ま}き{起|お}こす. The compound is {巻|ま}く (to wind, to roll) + {起|お}こす (to cause), and it is common in news writing.
